one_line_summary: [Zn(atz)(bdc)0.5] shows thermal_stability_up_to = 100.0 K for target gas

key_insights.title: Mechanism
key_insights.body: ATZ-bridged Zn chain and double-chain connectivity → stability

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [positive] use tetrazole-based organic linkers in MOF construction → supports construction of novel MOF networks due to strong networking ability

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [positive] combine ATZ and 1,4-benzenedicarboxylate (H2bdc) as mixed ligands → produces a photoluminescent metal-organic framework

key_insights.title: Comparison
key_insights.body: observed weight loss vs calculated weight loss: winner=tie on TGA_weight_loss_percent

key_insights.title: Comparison
key_insights.body: experimental powder X-ray diffraction pattern of compound 1 vs simulated powder X-ray diffraction pattern from single-crystal data of compound 1: winner=tie on PXRD_pattern_match

key_insights.title: Failure
key_insights.body: [performance_regression] heating the MOF above 220 °C: the ATZ and H2bdc organic ligands decompose and the whole framework collapses

notable_quotes: Thermal stability is limited: the TGA curve is unchanged only up to 100 °C, then 4.04% mass loss occurs from 100-130 °C due to water loss.
ATZ bridges Zn centers into 1D neutral double chains, and monodentate bdc carboxylates link these chains into the 2D framework.
PXRD shows the experimental pattern matches the simulated one from single-crystal data, confirming phase purity of compound 1.
